<!-- pr-reviewer: 2cd9d3d794991c4946414593e31468a70e35fabd -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: at the next minor cut).

### What looks good
- The toggle is off by default (`State::pick_through: false`, `crates/ui/src/state.rs:1841`), is not saved, and the only writer is the nav button's click arm (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewcube.rs:285-288`). The only reader is `feature_click::query_at` (`crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs:117`); no other viewport path sends `through: true`.
- "View state, not a command" matches its neighbours: Wire, Paths and Axes write their fields directly in the same `act` function, and the file header already says so. The decision record (`docs/decisions/692-pick-through-mode.md`) gives the reasons and the options that were dropped.
- Picks made with the toggle on go through the same selection path as any other pick. Only the query's `through` flag changes; the test reaches Contour1's source through the normal `op_click` route ("geometry selection updated for Contour1").
- The two behaviour tests prove what their names say. I checked by mutation in my local worktree only (nothing pushed): with `through` forced to `false`, `with_the_toggle_on_..._reaches_the_far_side_edge` fails; with it forced to `true`, `with_the_toggle_off_..._never_picks_the_edge` fails. Both tests reach the toggle through a real click on the nav button, so the wiring is covered end to end.
- The label is plain English ("Pick through: on/off"). No snapshot PNG is changed. The ui crate makes no Flecs calls. The new test file has a provenance line. No process files and no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. The body has a `Changelog:` line and `Refs #692` (partial: circle-centre picks wait on #759).
- `feat` is the right type, even though #692 is labelled `bug`: this adds a user control the issue asked for ("unless the user explicitly turns on a pick through mode, off by default and shown as such"). It is not a corrected behaviour.

### Local results (merged with `origin/main` 62a2c93a: already up to date, no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib --tests --no-run` | built |
| `egui_app::tests::pick_through` | 4/4 pass |
| `egui_app::tests::one_pick_rule` | 6/6 pass |
| `law_tests::view_cube_tests::the_hud_is_laid_out_from_the_pane_alone` | pass |
| camcraft-ui lib (CWD `crates/ui`) | 597 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| boundary / boundary_picks / feedback / fixtures / gpu_render / machine / models / operations / shell / theme_files (the quick-gate plan) | 3 / 6 / 6 / 7 / 11 (+1 ignored) / 6 / 4 / 31 / 20 / 14, all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **File size.** `viewcube.rs` grows from 459 to 478 lines; it was already over the ~400-line guide. This is not a blocker: open PR #1203 moves these buttons into `viewport_bar.rs` and trims `viewcube.rs` to 313 lines. Stacking is not needed, since both are `feat`s that merge at the cut. Merging #1203 first and then this PR (merge main, and move the `PickThrough` entry and its click/draw arms into the bar) keeps the second conflict small.
2. **Short panes clip the button.** `Hud::new` admits a 260 px pane. The sixth button sits at pane-top + 276..302 px, so in a pane shorter than about 302 px it is entirely outside the pane and takes no clicks. On main, Axes already overhangs at 260 px (bottom at 272 px). The risk: a user turns the mode on, then shrinks the pane, and cannot see or turn off the toggle. This is not a safety blocker, because a through-pick is still an explicit, highlighted selection. Suggested follow-up, best done with #1203's layout: derive the minimum pane height from `NAVS.len()`, or raise it, and pin it in `the_hud_is_laid_out_from_the_pane_alone` (`crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs:2111-2121`). That test still takes `Nav::Axes` as the bottom button, and its comment says "five buttons". It should check the last entry of `NAVS`.
3. **Discoverability.** The state text reaches the user only through the status line when they click. On main the nav buttons have no hover tooltips, so this matches its neighbours. A tooltip and AccessKit label for every nav button would be a small follow-up (P7).
4. **Test strength.** The "on" test asserts that the pick is a `Chain` but does not check that it is the hidden edge itself. The mutation check shows it still discriminates. Comparing the picked chain to the far-side edge would make the test self-explaining. The "off" test mostly repeats `one_pick_rule::a_click_over_a_hidden_edge_takes_the_near_face_or_nothing_never_the_edge` without that test's clearance assert. That is fine as a twin.
5. **Scope.** The toggle applies to every viewport feature pick: the operation page, the Setups page axis picks, and fixture locate. That fits #692's "one rule everywhere"; I am mentioning it so the hand check covers those pages too.

### Not exercised
- Nothing was looked at in a running app. I did not see the glyph's on/off drawing or the button's position.
- The pixel snapshot lane (release-lane by law) was not run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
